LargeST traffic flow over OpenStreetMap roads

This example is an offline reproduction bundle: the data/ folder contains the complete saved traffic snapshot (288 five-minute frames), downloaded OSM roads, water and place labels, and the source archive, tile checksums, dates and provenance of the downloads. Keep this folder, osm-figures.R and this R Markdown together. Install bdynets, jsonlite, knitr and rmarkdown once. Knitting requires no network, original HTML, HDF5 files, model fitting or browser execution.

library(bdynets)
source("osm-figures.R")
stopifnot(file.exists(params$snapshot))
snapshot <- read_traffic_data(params$snapshot)
stopifnot(snapshot$source == "largest")

Morning traffic in geographic context

The default is 08:00 on July 31, 2019 (one-based frame 97). Thin gray lines show downloaded OSM major roads from the zoom-9 basemap. Colored lines retain the original traffic display links, source quantile thresholds and directional offsets; these links are not map-matched road segments or inferred network adjacency. The background is a contemporary OSM extract, not a reconstruction of the road network in 2019. Both layers use Web Mercator. Labels are thinned for readability.

frames <- largest_osm_figures(snapshot, time_index=params$time_index)

Each region uses its own saved quantile thresholds: the same color need not mean the same flow in the two regions. Missing flow is gray. Values retain the source visualization’s saved precision; display-link values are endpoint averages and should not be treated as independent sensor counts.

Export figures and retain the selected data

This executable chunk creates a real relative directory, including parents, and checks that it is writable before opening graphics devices. Re-knitting replaces this example’s named exports. Change output_dir to preserve a run.

largest_osm_figures(snapshot, time_index=params$time_index,
                    output_dir=params$output_dir)
list.files(params$output_dir)
## [1] "bay-area.pdf"        "bay-area.png"        "input-checksums.csv"
## [4] "los-angeles.pdf"     "los-angeles.png"     "selected-frames.rds"
## [7] "session-info.txt"

Exports include PDF, high-resolution PNG, selected frames as RDS, input checksums and session information. The full traffic time series and OSM-derived responses stay in data/, so other time frames can be reproduced offline.

# Original viewer default: 16:10, one-based frame 195.
largest_osm_figures(snapshot, time_index=195L,
                    output_dir="output/largest-1610")

Data provenance

Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors, available under ODbL 1.0. The cached display geometry comes from the October 12, 2026 Protomaps build, an OSM-derived basemap distributed as an ODbL Produced Work. Geometry is simplified at zoom 9 and split at tile boundaries; it is suitable for map context, not routing or raw OSM network analysis. Water and place labels are cached too. download_osm.py documents the one-time download and skips existing extracts; normal rendering never calls it. To refresh deliberately, archive the old OSM files and run the script with Python 3, pmtiles, mapbox-vector-tile, requests and internet access. Daily upstream archives may expire; the committed local extracts are the reproducible source for these figures.

lapply(list.files("data",pattern="osm-provenance.json$",full.names=TRUE),
       function(path) {
         p <- jsonlite::fromJSON(path)
         p[c("source_url", "build_date", "retrieved_utc", "zoom",
             "sha256_uncompressed", "attribution", "limitations")]
       })
